claim: CREDO trains stated confidence on execution-graded code (DeepCoder train) with Qwen3-8B and reports AUROC, ECE and Brier on code, beating RLCR, DCPO and GRPO in domain.
stance_target: Row 11 / pivot 3 premise: no code study reports discrimination after training stated confidence (CLEAN provisional)
scope_conditions: Qwen3-8B only; Python code RLVR; evaluated on DeepCoder test, LiveCodeBench v5 and v6, HumanEval+; no probe arm
quoted_support: Code trains on DeepCoder and is evaluated on four: its in-distribution split, LiveCodeBench v5 and v6, and HumanEval+. We report accuracy and three calibration measures: ECE on the reported values, AUROC on the ranking they induce, and Brier on both.
numbers: Table 1 in-domain code CREDO: Acc .600, ECE .064, AUROC .850, Brier .127
RLCR code: Acc .553, ECE .075, AUROC .815, Brier .146
DCPO code: Acc .576, ECE .153, AUROC .776, Brier .153
GRPO code: Acc .581, ECE .182, AUROC .753, Brier .205
Base code: Acc .455, ECE .418, AUROC .690, Brier .395
DeepCoder 9,500 train problems; LCB v5 279, LCB v6 131, HumanEval+ 163 problems (Table 5)
